objects.original: A Borel probability μ on a finite-dimensional complete real Hilbert space, real-valued tests, and one fixed coefficient C. The cited Euclidean displays use ℝ^d and π.
objects.reconstructed: A probability μ on a finite-dimensional complete real inner-product space with its Borel σ-algebra, real-valued v and f, and C ∈ ℝ.
objects.evidence: CompactLogSobolevPoincare.lean:39–48 binds the real inner product, completeness, finite dimensionality, Borel measurable structure, IsProbabilityMeasure μ and C : ℝ. Choosing orthonormal coordinates identifies E with ℝ^d by a linear isometry, preserving the tests and gradient norms. The arbitrary Borel law is the authored formulation of the compact Euclidean implication, not a claim that Chewi states it verbatim outside the Langevin context.

domains.original: The premise and conclusion use C_c^∞ real functions. The target need not be centered; centering can destroy compact support. A noncompact square-root test needs its own justification.
domains.reconstructed: Both v and f are globally smooth and compactly supported, with no separate centeredness or integrability requirement.
domains.evidence: Chewi §2.1.1 (PDF pp.60–61) states both inequalities on C_c^∞(ℝ^d) and distinguishes density extensions. Lean:43–47 uses ContDiff ℝ ∞ and HasCompactSupport for both tests. Lean:49–79 forms bounded smooth g = f − ∫f dμ and uses Dg = Df to obtain compact support of the derivative, never of g. CompactGradientSqrtPerturbation.lean:42–92 gives pε ∈ [1/2,3/2], global smoothness of uε = √pε, uε ∈ L², integrable uε² log uε² and integrable squared derivative. Lean:110–116 converts the latter to ∇uε ∈ L² and uses LogSobolevCutoff.lean:187–217, whose compact smooth approximants and mass/entropy/energy limits license uε at the same coefficient.

quantifiers.original: For fixed E, μ and C, one LSI premise ranges over every smooth compactly supported real v; it implies the conclusion for every smooth compactly supported real f.
quantifiers.reconstructed: Fix E, μ and C; assume the displayed inequality for all v in C_c^∞, then conclude admissibility and the bound for every f in that class.
quantifiers.evidence: Lean:39–48 places hLSI's universal quantifier before the arbitrary conclusion test f. Neither v nor f is restricted to positive, mass-one or mean-zero functions. Exercise 1.7's centered f in the hint (PDF p.55, (1.E.1)) is a perturbation direction, not an added quantifier restriction on the Poincaré target.

assumptions.original: The compact smooth function-form LSI at 2C, on a Borel probability, with no supplied target integrability, centering, or sign restriction on C.
assumptions.reconstructed: Homogeneous entropy of v², written as ∫v² log(v²) dμ − m log m with m = ∫v² dμ and 0 log 0 = 0, bounded by 2C times squared-gradient energy.
assumptions.evidence: The expansion is the entropy convention referenced by §2.1.1 through Example 1.2.27. Lean:43–46 writes both terms and needs neither m > 0 nor a normalized v. Compact smooth v has continuous compactly supported v², v² log(v²) (continuous at zero), and squared-gradient norm, so these integrals are genuine on the probability law. Lean:49–56 derives ∫g dμ = 0 using μ(E) = 1. No density, reversibility, moment, 0 ≤ C, or C > 0 premise is present.

conclusion.original: For each compact smooth f, f, its centered square and its squared gradient norm are integrable; the variance is at most C times the gradient energy.
conclusion.reconstructed: Integrability of f, (f − ∫f dμ)² and ‖∇f‖² and the inequality between the two displayed integrals.
conclusion.evidence: Poincare.lean:24–39 defines variance and energy by exactly those integrals and Admissible by exactly those three Integrable predicates. Lean:49 proves integrability of f; :57–71 proves the centered square integrable by bounded L²; :72–79 and :124–126 prove genuine gradient-square integrability and return all three. The theorem does not use the separate Poincare.Satisfies predicate, whose nonnegative-C field is not part of this conclusion.

scopes.original: The authored compact Euclidean specialization of Exercise 1.7, with §2.1.1's test classes; no general closed-form/semigroup theorem or standalone probability-law KL expansion is asserted.
scopes.reconstructed: A function-form implication on a finite-dimensional Hilbert/Borel probability space, with compact smooth conclusion tests; no claim about a form closure, dynamics, or KL between laws.
scopes.evidence: PDF p.55 asks for direct linearization and gives a probability-KL hint; pp.60–61 supply the compact form, distinguish reversible-process notation and mention wider domains by density. Lean:89–117 normalizes the actual affine pε to mass one, uses uε² = pε, and cancels the integrated compensation in k(t) = t log t + 1 − t. The proof compares real integrals and only invokes the sufficient analytic cutoff domain; it does not identify Radon–Nikodym laws or assert a PI extension to a closed domain.

constant_dependencies.original: The LSI coefficient is 2C and the PI coefficient is the same underlying C, with no optimization, hidden factor, or sign requirement.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: The displayed premise has 2C and the displayed variance bound has C, both with squared-gradient energy.
constant_dependencies.evidence: PDF p.60 supplies the 2C_LSI and C_PI conventions, p.61 explicitly gives LSI(C) ⇒ PI(C), and (1.E.1) on p.55 supplies the entropy factor 1/2. Lean:76–82 uses the Riesz isometry and the genuine entropy and energy limits (1/2 and 1/4). Lean:83–130 divides only by ε² > 0, cancels the mass-one terms, and passes to the limit using continuity of multiplication by 2C for any real C. The resulting comparison is (1/2)Var ≤ (2C)(1/4)Energy, giving Var ≤ C·Energy without dividing by C.

review_evidence: Retrieved the primary PDF from https://chewisinho.github.io/main.pdf, independently hashed its 2,315,687 bytes to 8818e8fb40c07bd70651bafe10e8ec4500197c836928330b90025ca47da52fae, confirmed the August 20, 2026 edition, and read one-based PDF pp.55, 60–61 (printed pp.43, 48–49), with the entropy convention in referenced Example 1.2.27. Compared the authored statement and lesson formulas, the blind reconstruction, the complete on-disk CompactLogSobolevPoincare.lean (text identical to packet context; SHA-256 0ccc03c2c7ad30c9c6d6abfdbc6d0b711659095a37ca2eea1021eeb351962e09), and the Poincare, CompactGradientSqrtPerturbation, LogSobolevCutoff, BoundedDensityPerturbation and BoundedPerturbationEnergy definitions/proofs. The authored formula proof is valid: for t = εg with |t| ≤ 1/2, k(1+t) = t²∫₀¹(1−s)/(1+st) ds, so its quotient is dominated by g² and tends to g²/2; the energy quotient is H/(4pε) ≤ H/2 for H = ‖∇g‖² and tends to H/4. This exposition is a valid parallel argument, not a claim about the exact scalar tactics: Lean's entropy parent uses log t ≤ t − 1 and L’Hôpital, and its energy parent uses the weaker dominator H. The definitions, bounds, limits and conclusion agree; there is no semantic delta or repair. No prior audit or verdict was used and no build was run.
